statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the mobile entry, search-result, and error-recovery templates. Not covered: logged-in account, shopping/checkout, media playback, and every vertical tab because they are separate products/templates requiring authenticated or domain-specific runs.

page.framework: Mixed server-rendered pages with React/Fiber-powered result modules
page.notes: The host root resolves to the mobile Naver portal; search results are substantially server rendered (98% raw/rendered text coverage) with client-enhanced modules.

paths.description: Mobile entry surface and search starting point; represents the personalized portal reached at the host root.
Primary search journey and result-list template, exercised with the query “web platform”.
Invalid-route recovery template, used to judge HTTP/navigation failure handling.

findings.summary: Dark preference does not retint the interface
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a light gray/white interface and the page probe reports computed colorScheme “normal”.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare `color-scheme: light dark` and use preference-aware surface/text tokens via `prefers-color-scheme` or `light-dark()`.

findings.summary: Motion continues when reduced motion is requested
findings.evidence: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, four animations were still running (300–400 ms).
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or substantially simplify non-essential animation inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`.

findings.summary: Contrast preferences are not fully supported
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 3.36:1 tab text contrast and the page exposes no `color-scheme`; no forced-colors adaptation was evident in captured CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use system colors under forced colors, test `prefers-contrast`, and raise essential text/control contrast.

findings.summary: Primary state changes do not use View Transitions
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition declarations although the search/result state changes substantially.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for search state changes, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Autocomplete and information layers use custom overlay structures
findings.evidence: The results DOM contains multiple custom “layer” controls but zero `<dialog>`, `[popover]`, or `<details>` elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Move transient autocomplete/help layers to `popover` and modal flows to `<dialog>`, preserving accessible names and light-dismiss.

findings.summary: Reusable components do not show container-level adaptation
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe counted zero container-query rules across the rendered result page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use size container queries for result cards and horizontally reused modules instead of relying only on viewport rules.

findings.summary: Touch and keyboard affordances are too small or invisible
findings.evidence: The probe found 69 targets below 24 px in one dimension, including 3×16 px menu buttons; focus inspection found many links with `outline: none`, and Lighthouse failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24×24 CSS px target areas (prefer 44×44 for primary touch controls) and a visible `:focus-visible` indicator.

findings.summary: Mobile search results miss the Core Web Vitals performance bar
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 34.2 s, TBT 840 ms and CLS 0.166; the independent layout run measured CLS 0.327.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, reduce blocking work, and reserve stable space for asynchronously populated result modules.

findings.summary: Search results shift substantially during load
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer recorded CLS 0.327 across many shifts while skeleton/result content populated.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve final module dimensions and align skeleton geometry with loaded content; give media explicit dimensions.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 840 ms TBT; the layout observer saw a 236 ms long task and the trace saw three long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Break work into prioritized tasks, defer nonessential modules, and load expensive result features on demand.

findings.summary: The initial network payload is large and contains blocking dependencies
findings.evidence: HAR captured 119 requests and 5.68 MB, including 1.62 MB script, 774 KB fonts, and parser-inserted high-priority CSS/script candidates.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce critical CSS/font subsets, defer noncritical scripts, remove the HTTP redirect, and verify parser-inserted scripts use defer/module where safe.

findings.summary: Large JavaScript payloads dominate loading
findings.evidence: The HAR identifies a 914 KB vendor script and 238 KB main script; Lighthouse reports substantial unused JavaScript/CSS opportunities.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by result module, remove duplicate/legacy dependencies, and conditionally load AI, ads, and social integrations.

findings.summary: Interactive controls and images lack accessible semantics
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed ARIA allowed attributes, command names, link names, and image alt; the image probe found 33 of 50 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native controls where possible, remove invalid ARIA, give every command an accessible name, and provide meaningful or empty alt text.

findings.summary: Result navigation text fails minimum contrast
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 3.36:1 for 16 px search tabs against white, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken inactive tab text and validate all states against WCAG AA contrast thresholds.

findings.summary: Landmark and focus behavior is inconsistent
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark; the focus probe found numerous focusable links with no outline and an unlabeled text search input.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a single `<main>`, ensure logical headings, label the search input, and apply a consistent visible `:focus-visible` style.

findings.summary: Small targets undermine zoomed and touch use
findings.evidence: Although user scaling is allowed and no horizontal overflow occurred, Lighthouse failed target-size and the probe counted 69 undersized targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Enlarge hit areas without changing visual density and retest at narrow/zoomed layouts.

findings.summary: Image asset markup is incomplete
findings.evidence: The image audit found 23 images without width/height, 25 without responsive sources, and 5 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions, responsive `srcset`/`sizes`, and modern image formats from the image proxy.

findings.summary: Deprecated browser API usage remains
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated-API warning on the results page.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the deprecated API identified in DevTools/Lighthouse and prevent regressions in browser CI.

findings.summary: Indexing and link semantics are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports the results page blocked from indexing and four links with non-descriptive text, although all 316 anchors had hrefs and viewport metadata was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep intentional search-result noindex policy explicit, but make link text descriptive and ensure the public entry surface is crawlable.

findings.summary: Canonical/indexing signals are incomplete
findings.evidence: The results probe found no canonical or hreflang links, Lighthouse says indexing is blocked, and the root raw response contained only 88 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Define canonical policy for parameterized search URLs and ensure robots, sitemap, canonical, and host redirects agree.

findings.summary: Transport defenses and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: HTTPS and CSP are present, but HSTS and nosniff are missing; three cookies were not Secure and every observed cookie used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site behavior is essential.

findings.summary: The page has a broad third-party and tracking footprint
findings.evidence: Tracker capture saw 15 third-party origins including Facebook; the homepage HAR attributed 117/119 requests and 5.67 MB to origins outside the exact host.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary trackers, proxy or self-host first-party assets where appropriate, and defer analytics until consent/context requires it.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no HSTS, nosniff, or Permissions-Policy; frame protection and Referrer-Policy are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, nosniff, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; expand CSP beyond frame-ancestors for XSS-sensitive surfaces.

findings.summary: Images are not delivered with an efficient responsive strategy
findings.evidence: The image audit found no modern-format images, 25 images without srcset, 23 without dimensions, and six below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where effective, emit responsive candidates and dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: The page performs disproportionate network and background work
findings.evidence: The entry load made 119 requests/5.68 MB and included session, logging, AI, ad, and nudge requests plus multiple long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally initialize nonessential modules, batch telemetry, and deprioritize background fetches.

findings.summary: Third-party, image, font, and script weight is disproportionate
findings.evidence: HAR measured 2.95 MB images, 1.62 MB scripts and 774 KB fonts; tracker evidence found 15 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set template-specific byte/request budgets, subset fonts, optimize sprites/media, and defer third-party code until needed.

findings.summary: Repeated search-field interaction grows memory materially
findings.evidence: Across the repeated-focus probe JS heap rose from 55.2 MB to 89.9 MB and DOM elements rose 2,296→2,362; heap summaries differed by about 6 MB and 76k snapshot nodes. This is medium-confidence because background result modules may still be initializing.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile a settled baseline/target/final sequence, then release listeners, timers, caches, or result-module state retained after autocomplete closes.

findings.summary: The result page has a large initial heap footprint
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 1,406,829 snapshot nodes and 82.6 MB self size, including 95,861 closures and 11,549 FiberNode objects.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualize/defer below-fold modules and audit large React trees, closures, caches, and duplicated data for proportionality.
